newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Telecom groups to agree longest submarine cable.
newsitem.headline: Telecom groups to agree longest submarine cable.

text.p: Singapore Telecommunications (SingTel) said on Wednesday it had joined more than 80 other firms and telecommunication authorities to build the world's longest and largest-capacity submarine cable network.
SingTel said in a statement the cable would link the Pacific Rim, Southeast Asia, the Middle East and Europe at a total cost of US$1.3 billion.
SingTel said it would sign an agreement to finalise the investments in the cable with the other partners at a ceremony later on Wednesday.
It said the investors in the cable would, at a separate meeting on Thursday, award contracts worth a total of US$800 to begin contstruction of the submarine cable network.
SingTel said it had invested US$51 million in the network.
Other major investors in the project are Deutsche Telekom, British Telecom, Telekom Malaysia, Indosat, France Telecom, Telstra of Australia, China Telecom and Kokusai Densin.
A second will run 5,000 km between Singapore and Australia and the third will go 10,000 km from Singapore to various Asian destinations, including China and Japan.

The construction of the Singapore-Europe leg of the cable would be awarded to Alcatel, KDD-Submarine Cable Systems, AT&T Submarine Cable System Inc, a unit of AT&T and Maristel SpA of Italy, SingTel said.
It said the Singapore-Australia section would be built by Fujitsu and contracts for the two stretches were worth a total of US$800 million.
Construction of the first two portions would begin in the first quarter of 1997.
